trials.outcome: The single-agent MTD was 130 mg/m², infused over 2 hours every 3 weeks. Grade 3 pharyngolaryngeal dysesthesia, sensory neuropathy, and ataxia were dose limiting at 160 mg/m². A separate fixed-dose cohort at 85 mg/m² every 2 weeks reported no dose-limiting toxicity.

trials.role: Oxaliplatin monotherapy in Japanese adults with colorectal cancer
trials.outcome: Nine patients received 90 or 130 mg/m² by 2-hour IV infusion every 3 weeks. Sensory neuropathy of grade 1 or 2 occurred in all nine. The MTD was not reached at 130 mg/m², the highest dose tested.

trials.role: Early dose escalation of oxaliplatin monotherapy in adults
trials.outcome: Forty-four patients received 116 courses at doses of 45–200 mg/m². Cumulative sensory neuropathy was dose limiting. The highest dose studied was 200 mg/m².

trials.role: Non-tumoral liver pathology after oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy
trials.outcome: In a liver-resection series of patients with colorectal metastases, 34 of 43 patients treated with oxaliplatin-containing chemotherapy had marked sinusoidal alterations in non-tumoral liver. This was an observational study of combination regimens.

logp.method_description: The shake-flask method was utilized to measure the log Po/w values of the platinum complexes. Octanol and PBS used in this experiment were presaturated by incubation with shaking of the biphasic mixtures at room temperature overnight. 0.3 mL aliquots of PBS solution containing 50 μM Pt(IV) complex (cisplatin, carboplatin, oxaliplatin, 1a–d, 2a–d, 2a′–d′, 3a–d, and 3a′–d′) were incubated with the presaturated octanol (0.3 mL) in 2.0 mL tubes. To obtain homogeneous solutions, a 5 min vortex treatment was indispensable. After that, the two-phase mixtures were kept shaking at room temperature for 1 h to establish the partition equilibrium and then separated by centrifugation. After digestion, the platinum content in each phase was determined by ICP-OES. Each sample was tested in triplicate. The log Po/w values were expressed as the average of the results.

To measure Lipophilicity, log Po/w, the shake-flask method was used to obtain the amounts of each Pt complex in Water - Octanol [18]. 10 mg of Pt complex solved in 0.3 mL of water, pre-saturated with octanol, was incubated overnight at room temperature. After centrifuging, 0.3 mL pre-saturated octanol was added to supernatants, and the two-phase mixtures were kept shaking for 1 h to obtain the partition equilibrium, centrifugation was separately done and the Pt content in each phase was measured by ICP-OES. This data was obtained in triplicate. Table 1 shows the average log Po/w value.

Besides, we also tested the logP values of oxaliplatin, complexes 12 and complex 14 via shaking method and determined with HPLC instrument, using the same chromatographic conditions mentioned above. Firstly, the standard curves of oxaliplatin, compound 12 and complex 14 were obtained from HPLC and graphed with GraphPad 8.0. As for the assays of partition coefficient, oxaliplatin (50 mg) or complexes 12/14 (50 mg) was added into equilibrium glass bottles which containing a fixed mass ratio of deionized water (5 mL) and n-octanol (5 mL) then the solution was agitated for 12 h, 24 h or 36 h at 25 °C in dark. After that, the solutions centrifuged at 5000 r/min for 10 min, collected the upper or lower portion and diluted to desired concentration. The contents each portion were determined via HPLC instrument with the same chromatographic conditions mentioned above in section 4.9. Partition coefficient values were obtained via the formula: P=Co/Cw. Co represented concentrations 14 in n-octanol, while Cw represented concentrations in water.

The log P values were determined according to the OECD guideline using the shake-flask method [23]. Weighted amounts of platinum complexes were partitioned between an aqueous and 1-octanol phase. Platinum concentrations in the aqueous phase were measured by flameless atomic absorption spectrometry. Based on these results, the partition coefficients were calculated.

Values of log P (partition coefficient) were determined by using the shake-flask method. (20) Each platinum complex was dissolved in ultrapure water pre-saturated overnight with n-octanol. Then, the solutions were mixed with the same volume (950 μL) of n-octanol pre-saturated with ultrapure water overnight and shaken using a shaker for 15 min in a microtube. After shaking, the mixed solutions were centrifuged at 6000g for 5 min for phase separation, and the aqueous phase was diluted 1:1000 with 5% HNO3 and used for the determination of Pt concentration (Xw) by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP–MS). The data acquisition and processing were conducted with an Agilent 7500 series ICP–MS MassHunter workstation (G7200A; Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA, USA). The instrument settings were optimized for platinum (m/z 195). Thallium (m/z 205) was used as the internal standard. The Pt concentration of the aqueous solutions before equilibrium (Xw′) was also determined by ICP–MS using the same approach. The Pt concentration in the n-octanol phase (Xo) was calculated by subtracting Xw′ from Xw. Log P was calculated by using the following equation, log P = log{(Xw – Xw′)/Xw′}.

The cellular accumulation of a chemotherapeutic agent is often correlated with its lipophilicity, so we studied the lipophilicity (log D) of 3–6 by the shake-flask method in an octanol/water mixture (Fig. 5b). The lowest log D was observed for 3, while 6showed the highest log D value. Complexes 3–5 were more hydrophilic in the order of 3 > 4 > 5, whereas 6 was moderately lipophilic. This lipophilicity pattern does not correlate with higher cellular accumulation or better cytotoxicity. The cytotoxicity is the highest for 5 (oxamusplatin) and also 5 accumulates the most in cells, but it is more hydrophilic than 6. Complexes 3and 5 are quite different in terms of lipophilicity, yet they are more similar in terms of accumulation in cells. Complex 6 is a stable complex with lipophilicity within the range for better accumulation, but it shows lower accumulation in cells.

A shake-flask method was used to determine the log P values of the platinum complexes. Five micromoles of platinum complexes were dissolved in 2 mL of PBS buffer (pH = 7.4); a 0.5 mL solution of these platinum complexes was mixed with 0.5 mL of octanol that was presaturated with PBS buffer (pH = 7.4). The two phases were shaken at room temperature for 8 h and then separated by centrifugation. The platinum content in the two phases was determined by ICP-OES. The log P values were calculated from an average of three independent measurements.

The hydrophobicity (log P) of the series of compounds was determined using a shake-flask method (Albert, 1979). Aqueous (0.9% (w/v) sodium chloride (NaCl) and organic (n-octanol) phases were saturated for 1 week. Drugs were dissolved at a final concentration of 300 µM in the aqueous phase. An equal volume of saturated noctanol was added and the solutions mixed for 30 min (45 rpm). Samples were centrifuged (1500 g, 10 min) and the platinum content of the organic and aqueous phases determined by ICP-MS. The log of the ratio of platinum concentrations in the organic and aqueous phases were calculated to determine log P.

To determine the partition coefficients (P) of the investigated compounds, the “shake flask” method was used. Octanol-saturated water (OSW) and watersaturated octanol (WSO) were prepared using analytical grade octanol and ultrapure water. Platinum complexes were dissolved in OSW containing 200 mM NaCl and mixed with WSO in volumetric ratios of 2:1, 1:1, and 1:2. Mixing was done by vortexing for 30 min at room temperature to establish the partition equilibrium. To separate the phases, the samples were centrifuged at 3000g for 5 min. The layers were separated carefully using a fine-tip pipet and then analyzed for metal content by FAAS. The partition coefficients were calculated as a ratio of the concentration of the compound in the octanol layer to that in the aqueous layer [log P = log ([Pt]WSO/[Pt]OSW)].

The equal volume pre-treated n-octanol and aqueous solution were precisely measured and mixed, and the tested complex was slowly added to the solution until saturated, then shaken in a shaker for 48 h, and centrifuged at 2500 r/min for 15 min. The absorbance of the two-phase solution was measured by UV–Vis, and log Pow was calculated by formula (4-1).
